evidence.finding: Billing queue skill mappings were updated at 09:15, exactly when the incident began.
Billing staffing fell from 12 to 9 while General Service staffing rose from 19 to 22, with center-wide staffing unchanged.
Billing service level fell from 89.8% to 44.7% and ASA rose from 29.9 to 86.3 seconds, while General Service improved.
Scheduled and logged-in staffing remained at 49 agents, and productive staffing was essentially unchanged.
After incident onset, offered volume averaged only 1.8% above forecast, although Billing experienced a localized moderate increase.
Center service level declined from 88.4% before the incident to 76.5% during and after it.

primary_root_cause_detail: A Billing skill-mapping update at 09:15 redistributed three staffed agents from Billing to General Service. The resulting localized Billing capacity imbalance caused sharply higher waits and lower service level.
recommended_actions: Revert or correct the Billing skill-mapping change and restore the three-agent Billing allocation.
Validate Billing and General Service skill assignments before republishing routing configuration.
Monitor queue-level staffing, ASA, and service level after correction to confirm recovery.
Add change controls and automated alerts for offsetting queue-level staffing shifts after routing updates.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Center demand rose only 2.6% pre-to-post and averaged 1.8% above forecast; this does not explain the localized queue divergence.
Total scheduled and logged-in staffing remained constant at 49, with no material productive-staffing decline.
Aggregate AHT decreased 1.1%, Billing AHT decreased 0.5%, and post-onset AHT was below forecast.
No platform event was visible, and degradation was localized to Billing while other queues improved.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level decline was most likely caused by a 09:15 Billing routing change that shifted three agents to General Service. Billing then deteriorated sharply despite stable total staffing and near-forecast center demand; localized higher Billing volume amplified the impact.
